profile.summary:
I'm an AI research engineer in applied AI/ML with **4 years building agentic, generative and multimodal AI systems** across healthcare, finance, manufacturing and retail.

My work spans three areas:

- **Domain-adapted reasoning models**, built through fine-tuning and post-training with SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, SimPO, GRPO, GSPO and RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR).
- **Generative and multimodal solutions** across computer vision, NLP and deep RL, from research prototype to scalable production.
- **Production AI pipelines** with MLOps, AgentOps and LLMOps on AWS, Azure and GCP, with a focus on reliability, explainability and safety.

I enjoy working where multimodal models, deep RL and agentic systems meet, especially when research has a clear path to production, traceability and explainability are built in, and the result is greater human productivity.

experience.company: Axtria · Agentic AI Center of Excellence
highlights: Leading agentic AI engineering in Axtria's Agentic AI Center of Excellence.

Built an enterprise-grade agentic platform for legacy code transformation across languages, frameworks and cloud providers, using LangChain Deep Agents with a self-correcting orchestrator and 5 subagents (planner → diagnostic → remediation → execution → live test). Every repo runs in an isolated gVisor-sandboxed container.

Replaced vector-DB retrieval with Neo4j knowledge-graph traversal over import edges for cascade impact analysis: 94.2% migration accuracy (+23 pp over OpenRewrite), 79% lower LLM token cost, 92× faster planning, 2.1% rollback rate, with human-in-the-loop plan approval.

Developed a clinical decision support 7B VLM for Med-VQA, temporal diagnosis in radiology and pathology, and drug interaction analysis. Vision-guided chain-of-thought with a 4-stage pipeline (domain pretraining → SFT → DPO → GRPO) on 600K+ medical samples reached 90.4% VQA accuracy, +14.7% over LLaVA-Med. Deployed on Azure Container Apps with FastAPI and vLLM (4× faster inference) and real-time safety scoring.

Designed an agentic RL framework to fine-tune small language models on multi-tool trajectories: +30% task success, +40% tool-routing accuracy, 35% fewer invalid tool calls, with a trajectory memory that reuses past traces on unseen tasks.

Built a multimodal retrieval system for temporal video QnA with LangGraph agents, a knowledge graph and hybrid memory, grounding answers to any region or timestamp: +28% retrieval accuracy, 10× faster ingestion, 30% faster responses, 40% lower cost.
Built a real-time defect detection system for Genpact's Intelligent Fleet Management platform, training YOLO12 on 5K+ augmented 8K images with custom patch-based learning (78% precision/F1).
Optimised serving with a CPU-only sliced inference pipeline, cutting latency by 60% and deployment cost by 80%.
Researched image extraction and retrieval for multimodal RAG, published at IEEE ICECET 2024 and filed as a US patent.
Research on machine translation for low-resource Indian languages.
Worked on free-form text generation for content creators.

projects.title: Agentic Migration Foundry
projects.pitch: Upgrades entire legacy codebases on its own, and proves every change works before a human signs off.
projects.description: Framework, language and cloud-SDK migrations eat months of engineering time, and file-by-file copilots miss changes that ripple across a repo. AMF maps the whole codebase into a Neo4j dependency graph, plans the migration from it, then a self-correcting orchestrator and five specialist subagents diagnose, fix, run and live-test every change inside an isolated gVisor sandbox. Engineers review and edit the plan before anything executes.

metrics.label: migration accuracy vs 58.1% for GitHub Copilot (47 repos)

projects.title: TrialPilot
projects.pitch: Matches patients to the clinical trials they qualify for, with reasons a clinician can check.
projects.description: Eligibility criteria are long and full of negations and time windows, so manual screening is slow and keyword search misses patients. TrialPilot grounds every criterion to SNOMED CT, RxNorm and LOINC in a Neo4j trial knowledge graph, scores candidates with a fine-tuned decision model (Laya) plus neurosymbolic reranking, and gives the clinician a calibrated shortlist, not a verdict.

metrics.label: matching accuracy on 150 synthetic patient–trial pairs
lower cost with the fine-tuned model

projects.title: TheArxplorer
projects.pitch: Turns the daily flood of arXiv papers into a workspace you can ask questions.
projects.description: Save papers as they land, then ask across them. A LangGraph RAG pipeline decides whether each question needs your saved papers or the live web (Tavily, Firecrawl), and every answer comes back with citations. Users bring their own API keys, and every call is traced in LangSmith and Logfire.

projects.title: MedQwen-VGR1
projects.pitch: A 7B medical vision-language model that shows its reasoning on the image, not just an answer.
projects.description: Clinicians can't act on a black-box answer. MedQwen-VGR1 answers questions about radiology and pathology images, tracks a patient's scans over time and checks drug interactions, writing a step-by-step rationale grounded in the image regions it looked at. Trained in four stages (domain pretraining → SFT → DPO → GRPO) and served with vLLM on Azure with real-time safety scoring.

projects.title: Agentic RL for SLMs
projects.pitch: Teaches small, cheap language models to pick and call the right tools.
projects.description: Small models cost little to run but fumble multi-step tool use. This framework fine-tunes them with reinforcement learning on full multi-tool trajectories, and a trajectory memory lets the agent reuse what worked before when it meets a new task.

projects.title: Temporal Video QnA
projects.pitch: Ask a question about a video and get the exact moment, and the spot in the frame, that answers it.
projects.description: Long videos are hard to search. This system indexes video with LangGraph agents, a knowledge graph and hybrid memory, so each answer points to a precise timestamp and region.
